messages.author: af1128a04b090701
messages.subject: win_recycled frame clause
parts:
Hi,

is there a reason that win_recycled has frame specification? As far as I know, postgresql does not require it "select max(z) over()" is enough. On the other hand, Oracle cannot have frame specification without ORDER clause (this makes sense, but Oracle is not smart enough as PostgreSQL to actually check that frame is defined as undounded preceding/following).


win_recycled <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(x) {
    over(build_sql(sql(f), list(x)), partition_group(), NULL, frame = c(-Inf, Inf))
  }
}


I can create my own function by just deleting frame:

over(build_sql(sql(f), list(x)), partition_group(), NULL, NULL)

 but it would be great if this is in dplyr if there is no reason for such frame specification.

Tomas

messages.subject: Re: win_recycled frame clause
parts:
I cannot figure it out. 

Over last weeks I've spent many hours on Oracle backend for dplyr (https://github.com/tomasgreif/dplyrOracle/) (it took so long mainly because of my poor R-programming skills :)). Now, almost everything works with one exception being win_recycled. I understand that I need my own version of win_recycled, probably something like:

win_recycled_oracle <- function(f) {
  force(f)

  function(x) {
    over(dplyr:::build_sql(sql(f), list(x)), dplyr:::partition_group(), NULL, NULL)
  }
}

But how do I tell dplyr to use it when SQL is translated? I've tried to add it to `src_translate_env.src_oracle` with ` max   = win_recycled_oracle("max")`, but this is not the way (it is never actually used). Could you please give me a little more detail so I can fix this last major issue with dplyr backed for Oracle?

Tomas

messages.author: af1128a04b090701
messages.subject: Re: win_recycled frame clause
parts:
Ooooh, now it works. These is what I had to change:

- copied sql_translator and modified my window function. Fun fact - I had to put my win_recycled function physically before sql_variant. Otherwise, I got error "could not find function "win_recycled"" when running "load_all()". I have never seen this behavior before.
- after that I noticed that sql is still incorrect because of build_query(). There is the following line:

    from_sql <- build_sql("(", base_query$sql, ") AS ", ident(unique_name()),
      con = x$src$con)

- this is the only place where subquery is written in this way and unfortunately using "AS" is not supported by Oracle when naming subquery. As a result, I had to create a copy of build_query in my package.
- finally, I also had to create my own method for "update", even this was just a simple copy of the existing method for tbl_sql. Unless I did so, build_query in dplyr namespace was used.

Is there a reson for not using sql_subquery (for which I already have my own method) or I can file an enhancement request for dplyr?

Thank you for your help!


Dne pátek 3. dubna 2015 15:39:09 UTC+2 Hadley Wickham napsal(a):

You'll need to copy base_win() (found in translate-sql-base.R) and
modify it to use your win_recycled function.

Hadley
